content.text: Section 21 matches the preferred position closely. No hidden caps in warranty/indemnity sections, and "Fees" is a substantive recurring-revenue base.

input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
input.rationale: Section 21 meets the preferred position in full. (1) Cap: § 21.1 is expressly mutual ("each Party's total aggregate liability"; "The cap is mutual") and set at the greater of Fees "paid or payable" by Customer in the twelve months preceding the event and USD 1,000,000 — the exact basis and floor we require, using the preferred "paid or payable" formulation rather than "paid". (2) Cap base is not illusory: "Fees" (§ 1.5, p0007) means recurring subscription, professional services, usage and other Order Form amounts, i.e. substantive recurring revenue; the carve-out of a one-time implementation charge does not undermine the base, and the USD 1,000,000 floor protects against a low-fee first year. (3) Indirect damages: § 21.2 excludes consequential/indirect damages mutually ("neither Party"), and helpfully deems data-restoration, replacement services, breach notification and incident response costs to be direct damages — better than our position. (4) Carve-outs: "Excluded Claims" (§ 21.3) sits outside both the cap and the consequential-damages exclusion and covers every required item — breach of confidentiality, data-protection or security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement/misappropriation of the other Party's IP. So the § 20.1 IP indemnity, § 20.2 data-breach indemnity, and §§ 15–17 data/confidentiality/security obligations are all uncapped. (5) § 21.3 also confirms Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is not "damages" and is not limited by the section, as we require. No competing or one-sided cap is hidden elsewhere: searches for "liability" and "exceed" return only § 18 insurance limits and § 22 audit-cost language, and §§ 19–20 contain no aggregate-liability or sole-remedy cap (§ 20.5 adds a refund remedy "in addition to" Vendor's defence obligations). § 21.4 is standard savings language. No redline required.
